summary: Cynthia M. Beall is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. She studied at Pennsylvania State University (~1970–1976) and took up a post at Case Western Reserve University in 1976.

Cyril Henry Philips was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Liverpool and SOAS University of London. He served as Director of SOAS (1957) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of London (1972–1976).

Cyrus Stearns is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp, also studying under Turrell V. Wylie and several traditional teachers. He has served as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.
Cécile Ducher is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Matthew T. Kapstein and works there as a research fellow.

D. C. Lau was a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hong Kong under Xu Dishan and at the University of Glasgow, later holding posts at SOAS, University College London, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
D. C. Sarasvati is an Indologist who studied under V. Raghavan. She served as a Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras from 1964 to 1965.
D. Dennis Hudson was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He spent his career at Smith College (~1970–2004), where he served as a professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies.
D. L. Narasimhachar was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1927–1929), and served on the faculty at the University of Mysore from circa 1932 to 1962.

D. N. Shukla was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He earned a D.Litt. from the University of Lucknow under K. A. Subramania Iyer and held a post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1958).

D. Neil Schmid is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies under Victor H. Mair at the University of Pennsylvania, and also studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Waseda University.

D. Phillip Stanley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He has served as associate professor at Naropa University and Co-Director of Nitartha Institute.

D. R. Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and classics. After studying and teaching at Cambridge, he held positions at the University of Michigan and as Pope Professor of the Latin Language and Literature at Harvard University.

Dagfinn Føllesdal was a philosopher and linguist. He studied at the University of Oslo and Harvard University under Willard Van Orman Quine, later holding professorships at Stanford University (1968–2011) and the University of Oslo.
Dagmar Schwerk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Dorji Wangchuk from circa 2012 to 2017.

Daiei Kaneko was a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher. He studied at Otani University under Manshi Kiyozawa and later held academic posts at Otani University (~1916–1951) and Toyo University (~1925–1928).

Daijo Tokiwa was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora, later holding professorships at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, among other appointments.
Daiju Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University and held teaching posts attested in 2015 at Taisho University and Chisan Denpōin.

Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji. He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission, acted as interim abbot of San Francisco Zen Center, and founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center and Hokyoji Zen Practice Community.

Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki was a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher who studied at Waseda and Tokyo universities. He held academic posts at Gakushuin University, Otani University, and Columbia University, and founded the Eastern Buddhist Society and Matsugaoka Bunko.

Daishun Ueyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He studied under Akira Fujieda (~1958–1965) and served at Ryukoku University as an assistant professor (~1970–1977) and as president in 1983.
